title: Split three near-miss linux_configuration scripts under the 250-line cap
objective: Bring turn_off_auto_idle_screen_shutdown.sh (289), mtk_root/install.sh (262) and setup_gitea.sh (255) under the cap using the pattern established by the install_joplin.sh split, and prove the pattern holds on a small batch before scaling to the remaining 80 files.
acceptance_criteria: All three entry scripts and all three new libs are at most 250 lines.
bash -n and shellcheck pass on every entry script and every new lib, with no new suppression and no shellcheck disable directive.

A stubbed run of each entry script -- copied into a mirrored temp tree, with the final main invocation replaced by a declare -F probe -- reports every moved function as defined. This is the check that replaces the pass count; static checks alone are known insufficient.
No enforcement script is executed. turn_off_auto_idle_screen_shutdown.sh in particular manipulates idle inhibition and logind and must not run.
The two live systemd units that point at repo paths still resolve to existing files.
jscpd stays under its 2% duplication threshold on the real git commit, which is the only place it runs.
No behaviour change: functions move verbatim, apart from the two shellcheck findings fixed below.
out_of_scope: Executing any installer or enforcement step.
The digital_wellbeing scripts, which are live enforcement and are deferred to the end with phone_focus_mode.
Changing what any script does when run.
verifier: The scratchpad verify_split.sh per script (bash -n + shellcheck -x + stubbed run), plus systemctl cat on the two repo-path units, plus pre-commit run --files, plus the real git commit for jscpd.
